PullRequest.Title: Show the minimap slider while scrolling when showSlider is mouseover
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #127918

With `editor.minimap.showSlider: "mouseover"`, the minimap slider shows only while the pointer is over the minimap, so it can't be used to see where you are while scrolling the text.

## Change

- When the minimap gets a `scrollTopChanged` event with `showSlider: "mouseover"`, it adds a `slider-scrolling` class to its DOM node. A 500ms `RunOnceScheduler` removes the class after scrolling stops. This is the same delay the editor scrollbars use before fading.
- The CSS rule that makes the slider opaque on `:hover` also covers `.slider-scrolling`, so the existing 100ms fade applies.
- `showSlider: "always"` and the `autohide` modes are unchanged. `onDidChangeOptions` rebuilds the class name, so an options change clears the class.

## Testing

A scenario run opens a 1500-line file with `showSlider: "mouseover"`, keeps the pointer over the text, and scrolls with the mouse wheel. It checks that the editor really scrolled and that the minimap is not hovered, and samples the slider's computed opacity.

- Before (Insiders): opacity stays 0 while the editor scrolls 1500px.
- After (dev build): opacity reaches 1 while scrolling and is back to 0 1.2s after scrolling stops.

Scenarios.Scenario: Continuously scroll an editor with the default enabled minimap and `showSlider: "mouseover"`
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each changed scroll position synchronously reaches `Minimap.onScrollChanged`, ensures the `slider-scrolling` class is present, and resets a 500 ms timer before the already-existing minimap render is requested. No external operation must complete; browser style/compositor processing is the only added UI work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Added work scales with scroll-event frequency, not document line count or decoration count: one class-list operation and one timer reset per event. The slider is already layer-hinted and strictly contained.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One `RunOnceScheduler` exists per editor. Every scroll event cancels the previous timeout before creating the replacement, so at most one hide callback remains pending per editor and no callback burst accumulates.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or remote lookup is involved. Repeated class application is idempotent, while the single pending timer coalesces all events into one removal after scrolling stops.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the event path and per-event timer reset from the changed handler and `RunOnceScheduler.schedule`; high confidence that only one timeout remains pending and opacity targets an already composited, contained slider.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual wheel/trackpad event rates and browser timer costs vary, but the operation is constant-size and mirrors the existing scrollbar reveal debounce; there is no evidence of enough main-thread work to cause dropped frames.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The intended visibility update adds bounded O(1) UI work without layout reads, collection-wide work, unbounded retention, or concurrent timer buildup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Stop scrolling and allow the minimap slider to fade
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After 500 ms without another scroll event, the sole pending timeout removes `slider-scrolling`; CSS then performs the existing 100 ms opacity transition. This runs after scrolling and is off the active scroll critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost is constant per scrolling burst: one class removal and one opacity transition, independent of file size or number of scroll events in the burst.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Exactly one timeout callback can fire per quiescent scrolling sequence for each editor because each new event replaces the prior timeout.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The scheduled state itself provides coalescing; warm/repeated events replace the deadline rather than queueing callbacks. No cache keys or negative-cache states exist.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the scheduler implementation, CSS selector, and slider construction.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser compositing details vary, but the slider already has `translate3d` layer hinting and `contain: strict`, making a material layout or paint fan-out unlikely.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Deferred cleanup is bounded and occurs once after a burst.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create, reconfigure, and dispose editor instances
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Construction now allocates one scheduler and closure per editor; changing minimap options rebuilds the minimap class name, and disposal synchronously cancels any pending scheduler timeout through the registered disposable.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Memory grows by one small scheduler/closure per live editor and is released with the editor. It does not grow with scroll history or document size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One scheduler per live editor; no background worker, IPC, filesystem, network, or subprocess concurrency is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. Option changes reset the class state, and lifecycle registration owns timer cancellation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from constructor registration and `RunOnceScheduler.dispose` cancellation behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact object size is runtime-dependent, but the fixed per-editor allocation is too small to establish meaningful startup or memory degradation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The eager allocation is constant and correctly lifecycle-bound, with no leak or retained history.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete two-file diff and traced scroll dispatch, DOM mutation/compositor behavior, timer scheduling/coalescing, option changes, and disposal. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced, and the PR does not itself fix a separately evidenced shipped performance regression.
